podcast.title: Madison Square Garden Concert Reception (1971)
podcast.body: In the fall of 1971, Rick Nelson and his band performed at a nostalgic multi-act concert at New York's Madison Square Garden, sharing the bill with classic rock and rollers like Chuck Berry, Bo Diddley, and Bobby Rydell. Nelson and his band were poorly received by the "hippie crowd," who reportedly "sat on their hands" and even booed. This negative experience led Nelson to storm off stage and write his hit song "Garden Party." "But Rick Nelson and his band were not well received. The hippie crowd in attendance mostly sat on their hands, reportedly some even booed."

srcs.source: Hit Parade Music History and Music Trivia

podcast.title: Band Influence for The Cramps
podcast.body: Ricky Nelson was mentioned as an influence for The Cramps, alongside other rockabilly and early rock and roll artists, underscoring their embrace of primitive 1950s sounds. "También eran influencias para la banda Ricky Nelson, Roy Orbson, Jassie Latkins o Lingray."

srcs.source: Central Sonora
srcs.episode: Amor, Terror y Psychobilly: La Historia de The Cramps

podcast.title: Booed at Madison Square Garden
podcast.body: In October 1971, Rick Nelson and his Stone Canyon Band were booed by fans at Madison Square Garden during a "Rock and Roll Spectacular" (renamed from "Rock and Roll Revival"). Fans, who expected his 1950s hits and image from "Ozzie and Harriet," rejected his country rock sound, long hair, boots, and bell-bottom jeans. Nelson believed the booing was directed at him for his changed musical direction and appearance. "So they booed him and his long hair to the point that Randy Meisner, who would leave the band and go help create something else called the Eagles, left."

srcs.source: For the Record - The 70s
srcs.episode: Ep. 35 - Cosmic American Music - 70s Country Rock

podcast.title: Changing Image and Musical Direction
podcast.body: Nelson's appearance, featuring boots, bell-bottom jeans, and shaggy hair, clashed with the 1950s Ricky Nelson image that fans from "Ozzie and Harriet" expected at the 1971 Madison Square Garden concert. He had been making country-tinged music since the mid-1960s, so his new material shouldn't have been a complete surprise, yet it was met with strong resistance. "They wanted Ricky Nelson from the Ozzy and Harriet show of the 50s, not Rick Nelson with boots and bell-bottom jeans and shaggy hair."

srcs.source: For the Record - The 70s
srcs.episode: Ep. 35 - Cosmic American Music - 70s Country Rock

podcast.title: Early TV/Pop Star Hybrid
podcast.body: Ricky Nelson in the 1950s is cited as an early example of an artist who successfully combined a TV star image with a pop music star image, a model later followed by artists like David Cassidy and Shaun Cassidy. "In the tradition of Ricky Nelson in the 1950s and Sean Cassidy's brother David Cassidy Sean Cassidy combined this TV star with pop music star image."

srcs.source: For the Record - The 70s

podcast.title: Image Reinvention Attempt
podcast.body: Ricky Nelson, even before the 1970s, attempted to change his image from a teenage idol to appeal to a broader audience. As part of this effort, he changed his name from Ricky to Rick Nelson, a difficult transition for many teenage idols. "Even thinking back to well before the 70s what Ricky Nelson tried to do and even changing his name from Ricky to Rick Nelson That's not easy."

podcast.title: Image Reinvention Effort
podcast.body: Rick Nelson adopted this name as part of an effort to transition from his earlier identity as a teenage idol, Ricky Nelson, to broaden his audience. This name change was part of a difficult process for him to alter his public image. "Even thinking back to well before the 70s what Ricky Nelson tried to do and even changing his name from Ricky to Rick Nelson That's not easy."

podcast.title: Imperial Records Teen Idol
podcast.body: Ricky Nelson was a new teen idol star for Imperial Records who was in need of new material. "Imperial Records, who had a new teen idol star who needed material."

srcs.source: A History of Rock Music in 500 Songs

podcast.title: Later Reliance on Old Hits
podcast.body: Ironically, a decade after being booed for his new country rock sound, Rick Nelson began putting on shows that relied on his old hits and their more familiar arrangements. This pivot suggests an eventual capitulation to audience expectations for nostalgia. "Ironically, a decade later, he would be putting on shows that relied on his old hits with their more familiar arrangements."

srcs.source: For the Record - The 70s

podcast.title: Teen Idol Ricky Nelson
podcast.body: Rick Nelson was known as "Teen Idol Ricky Nelson" in the 1950s before evolving his musical style. "In the fall of 71, Nelson, known in the 50s as Teen Idol Ricky Nelson, was invited to play a nostalgic multi-act concert at New York's Madison Square Garden."

podcast.title: Unexpected Hit and Rock and Roll Promotion
podcast.body: He achieved an unexpected hit after singing on his parents' TV show, which resulted in him being rapidly promoted as a rock and roll star. "Vicki Nelson had had an unexpected hit after singing on his parents' TV show, and as a result he was suddenly being promoted as a rock and roll star."
